title: Robust Jailbreak Detection in Large Language Models Using Behavioral Fingerprinting
reason: Jailbreak detection is the central problem, and the study proposes behavioral fingerprinting for multi-turn interactions. It reports experimental comparison against baselines with an F1-score, providing direct evidence on detection and defense.

title: A Comprehensive Security Framework for the Model Context Protocol (MCP) in Multi-Agent AI Systems
reason: Prompt injection is one of several security threats addressed in an MCP-focused multi-agent security framework. The work is relevant to agent security and mitigation, but the abstract does not describe a prompt-injection-specific evaluation.

title: RAG-Augmented Payroll Intelligence Stack: A Zero-Trust, Policy-Verified Architecture for Compliant and Explainable Payroll Automation
reason: The study evaluates a policy-bounded RAG architecture on a benchmark and explicitly reports prompt-injection robustness among its outcomes. Prompt injection is not the sole focus, but the RAG context and evaluated security architecture are directly useful to the review.

title: Mitigating Prompt Injection Attacks in ModelAgnostic Networks (MAN)
reason: Prompt injection mitigation is the central focus. The proposed model-agnostic detection framework is tested on more than 8,000 prompts across multiple model families and reports precision and F1 results against baselines.

title: Security Risks and Privacy Challenges of Large Language Models in Enterprise Environments
reason: Controlled experiments assess susceptibility to prompt injection and role-based manipulation in enterprise data scenarios, with observed leakage and compliance failures. The paper also proposes mitigation guidance, although prompt injection shares focus with broader privacy and compliance risks.

title: Siren: A Learning-Based Multi-Turn Attack Framework for Simulating Real-World Human Jailbreak Behaviors
reason: The study centrally proposes and evaluates a learning-based multi-turn jailbreak attack framework. It reports attack success rates across attacker and target LLMs and compares against single-turn and multi-turn baselines.

title: MAJD: Intent-Aware Multi-Agent Framework for Jailbreak Defense
reason: Jailbreak defense is the core contribution. The multi-agent framework targets single-turn and multi-turn attacks and is evaluated across several attack methods and target models, directly informing defense and detection questions.

title: MELF: Multi-Agent Evaluation for LLMs Fairness Based on Hierarchical Genetic Algorithm
reason: The primary goal is fairness evaluation, but the method uses transferable adversarial prompts, reports jailbreak attack success, and analyzes attack mechanisms and model vulnerabilities. This gives partial but meaningful evidence on adversarial prompting and jailbreak behavior.

title: Prompt Engineering for Large Language Models: Zero-shot, Few-shot, and Beyond
reason: The paper primarily synthesizes prompt-engineering methods and proposes a taxonomy and evaluation blueprint. Prompt injection and poisoning are treated as security concerns within a broader prompt-engineering scope, making the contribution relevant but not central to the review.

title: An Experimental Evaluation of Prompt Injection Attacks on LLM-Based Content Moderation Systems
reason: Direct prompt injection attacks are the central subject, with controlled experiments across three LLMs in a content-moderation application. The study examines robustness differences and the effect of attack variations, although the abstract gives limited quantitative detail.

title: LLM-based Cybersecurity Honeypots Evaluation Metric Development and Persona Shaping via Structured Prompt Engineering
reason: Prompt injection is identified as a vulnerability of LLM honeypots, but the main contributions concern persona shaping, evaluation metrics, and model selection. The experiments are substantial for the application, yet the abstract does not show a focused analysis of prompt-injection attacks or defenses.

title: Partial-Reps: Defending Large Language Models against Jailbreaks via Partial Repetition
reason: The paper directly proposes a jailbreak defense intended to reduce the cost of self-querying detection. It is evaluated on eight benchmark datasets and three LLMs, providing direct empirical evidence on defense effectiveness and efficiency.

title: SecureRag: Preventing Sensitive Information Leakage In Rag Pipelines
reason: The work proposes and evaluates a RAG defense framework against sensitive-data leakage, explicitly testing prompt injections alongside other adversarial scenarios. Its RAG setting, filtering defenses, synthetic datasets, multiple models, and attack tests make it highly relevant.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning for Offensive Security: Towards Robust LLM Agents for CTF Automation
reason: The main contribution is a retrieval-first LLM agent for CTF automation, with benchmark evaluation focused on task completion and reasoning stability. Prompt injection is mentioned in the threat model, but the abstract does not indicate a dedicated attack or defense evaluation.

title: A Real-Time Framework for Prompt Injection Attacks Detection on Cloud-Hosted Large Language Models
reason: Prompt injection detection is the central focus. The paper proposes a real-time DistilBERT-based detection and blocking framework and reports extensive comparisons on precision, latency, and deployment cost in a cloud environment.

title: Enhancing AI Security through CIA+
reason: Prompt injection is listed among several AI-specific threats motivating a broader extension of the CIA security model. The work appears mainly conceptual and framework-oriented, with no prompt-injection-specific experiment or structured empirical evaluation described.

title: Image-based Prompt Injection: Hijacking Multimodal LLMs through Visually Embedded Adversarial Instructions
reason: Image-based prompt injection is the central phenomenon. The paper presents an end-to-end black-box attack pipeline and evaluates multiple adversarial strategies and embedding configurations, reporting attack success under stealth constraints.

title: Evaluating Multi-Agent Defences Against Jailbreaking Attacks on Large Language Models
reason: The study directly evaluates multi-agent defenses against multiple jailbreak strategies. It compares single-, two-, and three-agent configurations and reports security trade-offs including false negatives, false positives, and computational overhead.

title: Prompt Injection Detection and Mitigation with AI Multiagent NLP-based Agentic Frameworks
reason: Prompt injection detection and mitigation are the central contributions. The multi-agent framework is empirically evaluated on 500 engineered injections across ten categories and introduces several attack and mitigation metrics.

title: Predicting Trust Risks in Al-Generated Educational Feedback: A Technical Framework Using Simulated Threats and System Logs
reason: Prompt injection is one of three simulated trust-failure types modeled in AI-generated educational feedback. The study creates labeled cases and trains interpretable classifiers, offering useful but partial evidence on proactive detection because the broader focus also includes semantic drift and evasiveness.
